text.title: llamaindex-hybrid-retrieval Core Rules
text.summary: Rules for LlamaIndex hybrid retrieval: QueryFusionRetriever, cross-encoder reranking, AutoMergingRetriever, similarity thresholding.

rule.statement: Use QueryFusionRetriever(mode='reciprocal_rerank') to combine ≥2 retrievers (vector + BM25). Set num_queries=1-4 based on rerank budget.
rule.rationale: RRF is more stable than weighted sum; num_queries beyond 4 burns LLM calls for diminishing returns.

rule.statement: Pre-rerank pool size (fusion_top_k) must be at least 4x the post-rerank size (rerank_top_n). A rerank over 3 candidates is a no-op.
rule.rationale: Rerank needs a real candidate set to discriminate; tiny pools defeat the purpose.

rule.statement: Apply SimilarityPostprocessor BEFORE the cross-encoder rerank to pre-filter low-relevance candidates. Run rerank on the survivors only.
rule.rationale: Pre-filtering cuts rerank cost 3-5x without recall loss when threshold is calibrated.

rule.statement: Calibrate similarity_cutoff threshold on your own eval set per-query-class. Never reuse a threshold from a different corpus or benchmark.
rule.rationale: Thresholds do not transfer; cross-corpus reuse silently drops recall on niche queries.

rule.statement: Cap QueryFusionRetriever concurrency with num_workers=4-8 or wrap in asyncio.Semaphore(8). Default is unbounded.
rule.rationale: Unbounded fusion opens N times k concurrent LLM calls — straight into rate-limit cliffs.

rule.statement: For hierarchical corpora, wire AutoMergingRetriever to promote a parent node when ≥half its children match.
rule.rationale: AutoMerging is designed for tree-structured corpora; using it on flat corpora adds latency without lift.

rule.statement: Choose a distilled cross-encoder (e.g., ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) for latency-sensitive deployments; reserve full BERT-class rerankers for offline pipelines.
rule.rationale: Distilled rerankers run sub-100ms on CPU; full BERT crosses 500ms.

rule.statement: Always A/B hybrid vs vector-only on a labeled eval set before shipping. Hybrid adds latency and complexity; the lift must be measurable.
rule.rationale: Without an eval set you cannot justify hybrid's added latency cost.

rule.statement: When corpus_heterogeneity is high (prose plus keyword-exact chunks such as product codes) AND latency_target_ms is tight (below 1000 ms but at or above the 500 ms Skip-If floor), the hybrid-retriever-spec MUST fuse VectorIndexRetriever + BM25Retriever through QueryFusionRetriever(mode='reciprocal_rerank') with num_queries=1 (no LLM query generation), fusion_top_k=20, SimilarityPostprocessor pre-filter (r3, r4), then SentenceTransformerRerank with a distilled cross-encoder (cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 or equal) and rerank_top_n=5, and record per-stage timings with rerank under 300 ms. num_queries greater than 1 and BERT-base or larger rerankers are forbidden on this branch; if the measured p95 still misses latency_target_ms, drop the reranker before dropping BM25.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (QueryFusionRetriever, SentenceTransformerRerank); Sentence-Transformers MS MARCO cross-encoder model cards

rule.rationale: Every generated sub-query is one LLM round trip plus one more retrieval pass per retriever, so at a sub-second budget num_queries=1 is the only setting that leaves room for a rerank at all. A full-size cross-encoder on CPU is what turns 400 ms into 2.5 s (fm-02); the distilled MiniLM model keeps the rerank stage inside the 300 ms stage budget.

rule.statement: When corpus_heterogeneity is high AND latency_target_ms is relaxed (1000 ms or more), the hybrid-retriever-spec MUST fuse VectorIndexRetriever + BM25Retriever through QueryFusionRetriever(mode='reciprocal_rerank') with num_queries between 2 and 4 chosen from rerank_budget_usd (r1) and num_workers capped at 4-8 (r5), fusion_top_k between 20 and 30 with rerank_top_n=5 so the pool is at least 4x the output (r2), SimilarityPostprocessor with a cutoff calibrated on the project's own eval set (r4) before the cross-encoder, and an A/B against the vector-only baseline recorded in the spec (r8). Weighted-sum fusion and a rerank pool under 4x rerank_top_n are forbidden on this branch.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (QueryFusionRetriever, BM25Retriever); Cormack, Clarke and Buettcher, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, SIGIR 2009

rule.rationale: Mixed corpora are exactly where BM25 catches the exact-token hits the embedder paraphrases away, and RRF is the fusion that does not need per-retriever score normalisation. The 4x pool rule exists because a rerank over 3-5 candidates cannot reorder anything (fm-01); with a relaxed budget there is no reason to starve it.

rule.statement: When corpus_heterogeneity is low (homogeneous prose, no keyword-exact identifiers to match), the hybrid-retriever-spec MUST NOT wire QueryFusionRetriever or BM25Retriever at all: the retriever is a single VectorIndexRetriever with similarity_top_k=20, followed by SimilarityPostprocessor with a calibrated cutoff (r4) and a distilled cross-encoder rerank to rerank_top_n=5 (r7). The spec MUST include the A/B of rerank-on vs rerank-off on the labeled set (r8); if the lift is not measurable the reranker is removed and the record says vector-only.
rule.rationale: Vector retrieval already covers paraphrase on uniform prose, so a keyword leg adds 200-400 ms and a second index to keep in sync for hits it will not find. What can still lift a homogeneous corpus is reranking the top-20, and that is cheap enough to test and drop honestly rather than carry unproven.
